title: Wittmann wins as Wickens is disqualified at the Red Bull Ring
dek: Marco Wittmann won at the Red Bull Ring to lead a BMW 1-2-3-4, after pole-sitter Robert Wickens was black-flagged from the lead for ignoring a drive-through penalty.

chapters.title: Wittmann arrives with a 20-point cushion
text: The sixth round of the ten-race 2014 DTM season moved from Russia to Austria, where the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg hosted the series on Sunday 3 August. Three weeks earlier at Moscow Raceway BMW rookie Maxime Martin had taken his first pole and his first win, while Marco Wittmann’s fourth place was enough to stretch his lead in the drivers’ table to 70 points, 20 ahead of Mattias Ekström, with Bruno Spengler and Edoardo Mortara tied on 41 and Mike Rockenfeller on 35.

Moscow had also hurt Audi, whose Rockenfeller and Adrien Tambay had collided on a safety car restart, and left Mercedes-Benz without a car in the top six. The Red Bull Ring offered a chance to change the picture on a 4.326-kilometre circuit, over a distance of 47 laps and a mandatory stop in a pit window that opened on lap 16 and closed on lap 31. Robert Wickens, the Norisring winner, was the Mercedes driver most likely to take the fight to BMW.

chapters.title: Wickens snatches pole from Glock by six thousandths
text: Qualifying was decided on the very last lap. Augusto Farfus was quickest in the first segment, but in the final shoot-out it was Timo Glock who seemed to have pole, with BMW’s Wittmann and Farfus behind him. Wickens had spun, yet he put everything together after the chequered flag had come out and took pole with 1:25.175, only 0.006 seconds ahead of Glock’s 1:25.181. Glock said it hurt, having seen himself first on the video screens during his cool-down lap.

Wittmann was third on 1:25.228, 0.053 seconds off the pole, and Farfus fourth. Pascal Wehrlein put a second Mercedes on the third row in fifth, ahead of Jamie Green, the only Audi to reach the final segment and sixth. Christian Vietoris was seventh and Moscow winner Martin eighth, with Joey Hand ninth and Spengler tenth. Martin Tomczyk was 11th.

It was a bad day for Audi. Ekström, second in the championship, was only 16th and said his car had simply lacked pace although he had made no big mistakes. Nico Müller was 18th, and Tambay, Mortara, Gary Paffett, Vitaly Petrov and Paul di Resta were all knocked out in the first segment, Di Resta ending up 23rd.

chapters.title: Wickens holds Farfus at bay
text: Wickens got away perfectly from pole and kept the lead while Glock and Farfus chased. Farfus took second from fellow BMW driver Glock at the hairpin on lap 5 and then began to close, attacking Wickens side by side on several laps and backing up a tight queue behind them. Wittmann, meanwhile, made a poor start and fell several places, a mistake he later admitted was his own.

Behind the leaders the stewards were busy. António Félix da Costa stopped early on, and around lap 15 five drivers, among them Mortara, Hand and Martin, were sent through the pit lane for yellow-flag infringements. Hand and Martin finished 12th and 14th and Mortara 16th, out of the points.

chapters.title: Green leads, Wickens is told to come in
text: Farfus was the first of the leaders to stop and Wickens followed a few laps later, with Glock beside him in the pit lane. Glock’s BMW Team MTEK crew was a touch quicker, and Wickens was released into the space in front of him, forcing the German to brake. The stewards called it an unsafe release and handed Wickens a drive-through penalty.

The stops also elevated Jamie Green, who pitted later than the rest and briefly led the race. His joy ended when it emerged he had kept the option tyres on a lap too long, and the Audi was given a drive-through of its own. Audi’s DTM boss Dieter Gass said a communication problem was behind the late call. Farfus passed Wickens for the lead, and Wickens took it back.

chapters.title: The leader is shown the black flag
text: Wickens did not serve the penalty. Mercedes argued with race control, saying the stewards had confused Wickens’ car with that of Wehrlein, who had also been involved in an incident in the pit lane, and kept him out. After several laps without a visit to the pits the black flag was shown, and Wickens came in on lap 34 to end the race, ending in a disqualification.
Wehrlein, running fourth for a time, was out after 26 laps. As Wickens and Green fell away, Wittmann went to work, passing Glock and then Farfus and taking over the lead once the Mercedes was out.

chapters.title: A BMW 1-2-3-4
text: Wittmann led the final laps and took his third win in six races in 1:08:23.185. Farfus was second, 3.298 seconds behind, with Glock third at 5.391 seconds and Martin Tomczyk fourth, completing a BMW 1-2-3-4 with one driver from each of the four BMW teams. Timo Scheider drove from 14th on the grid to fifth for Audi, 6.666 seconds behind, and Tambay climbed from 20th to sixth.

Ekström started 15th and finished seventh, passing Vietoris and Green late on, and Green recovered from his penalty to eighth. Vietoris took ninth, the only Mercedes in the points, and Spengler was tenth. Rockenfeller set the fastest lap, a 1:25.266 on lap 45, but he had started 17th and came home 13th.

chapters.title: Wittmann is 39 points clear with four races left
text: Wittmann said the race had not been as easy as it looked: he had got away very badly, fought back and then had very good pace on the primes in the second stint, setting the fastest lap on primes on his penultimate lap. He added that he felt “just really lucky”. BMW Motorsport Director Jens Marquardt called the result historic: BMW had never before filled the top four places since returning in 2012, and the last time it happened in the DTM was at Hockenheim in 1992.

Mercedes was furious. Wolfgang Schattling said Wickens could certainly have won and that the penalty was not justified, claiming the stewards had mistaken one car for the other. Glock took a different view, saying Wickens had left him no room and that he had to brake to avoid the wall or the Mercedes, though he conceded the verdict was the stewards’ to give. Gass said Audi had lost the race in qualifying, and also pointed to the communication problem that cost Green.

The result tightened Wittmann’s grip on the title. He now has 95 points, 39 ahead of Ekström on 56, with Spengler on 42, Mortara 41, Tambay 36 and Rockenfeller 35. Spengler is 53 points behind the leader and Mortara 54. BMW also went top of the team and manufacturers’ tables.

With four races left the DTM travels to the Nürburgring on 17 August. Marquardt said the performance weights were bound to make that a real challenge for BMW, and Scheider hoped fifth place would mark the turnaround in a disappointing season. Rockenfeller, who set the fastest lap, left with only a 13th place, while Ekström’s seventh left him chasing the leader from a long way back after a day on which neither Audi nor Mercedes could keep up with the BMWs at the front.

facts.t: Wittmann’s third win in six races
facts.v: Marco Wittmann won in 1:08:23.185 over 47 laps, 3.298 seconds ahead of Augusto Farfus, after dropping back at the start.
